newsitem.title: POLAND: Philip Morris to boost Polish investment.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris to boost Polish investment.

text.p: Philip Morris said Monday it wants to increase investment at its cigarette-producing plant in southern Poland to more than $200 million from earlier planned $145 million.

"When we purchased the Krakow plant ... our investment commitment was $145 million over the next three years. We now project the investment to exeed $200 million," the plant's president, Andre Calanzopoulos, told a news conference.

Philip Morris agreed early last year to pay $372 million for a controlling stake in the country's biggest cigarette producer, Zaklady Przemyslu Tytoniowego Krakow SA, which has a 30 percent share of Poland's lucrative tobacco market.
Calanzopoulos said he was satisfied with the Polish market even though officially registered cigarette consumption dropped last year by about 7 percent to 90 billion.
Even if the Polish cigarette market continues to fall, Philip Morris will try to boost sales by gaining market share at the expense of its rivals, he said.
But Calanzopoulos said real consumption of cigarettes last year was likely to have been higher as it was fed by cross-boder smuggling.
The smuggling was likely to increase if the finance ministry continued to boost the excise tax on tobacco products, he said.
